newsitem.title: USA: Kestrel Energy to start exploratory drills.
newsitem.headline: Kestrel Energy to start exploratory drills.

text.p: Kestrel Energy Inc said Monday it plans to start three wells in August as part of a new exploratory drilling program.

The first well targets the Daisy Prospect in California's San Joaquin Basin. Kestrel said that based on seismic data, sands in the prospect have the potential to contain up to 38 billion cubic feet of gas, if gas is present.
The company also plans to drill the Greer Prospect in the San Joaquin Basin, a prospect that Kestrel said could contain up to 20 million barrels of oil.

Kestrel said it also will start drilling on the Longhorn Prospect in the Offshore Carnarvon Basin of Western Australia. The drilling will test a sandstone reservoir that could contain up to 32 million barrels of oil wil, Kestrel said.

Kestrel is an oil and gas exploration and production company that is headquartered in Denver and that has producing properties in California, Kansas, Louisiana, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Texas and Wyoming.
